description.value: The study investigated the influence of heavy drinking and family history of alcoholism on alcohol cue-related BOLD fMRI response among college students.

spans.text: We investigated the influence of heavy drinking and family history of alcoholism on alcohol cue-related fMRI response among college students.

value: we predicted that 1) heavy drinkers would show greater BOLD response than light drinkers to alcohol images, relative to non-alcohol images, in reward-related regions including NAcc and medial frontal cortex, 2) FHP would show greater response than FHN individuals in these reward-related regions, and 3) there would be an interaction between family history of AUD and personal drinking on BOLD response to alcohol-related cues, such that enhanced cue reactivity among FHP would be more apparent in light drinkers than in heavy drinkers.

value: Heavy drinkers demonstrated greater BOLD response contrast to alcohol picture repetition, defined as greater response to the second presentation than to the first presentation, than light drinkers in frontal, insular, temporo-parietal, occipital, and temporal regions. Light drinkers showed the opposite pattern, with less response during the second presentation than during the first presentation. This greater repetition-related cue response among heavy drinkers may contribute to the maintenance and amplification of problematic drinking.
